reference: Richard, M., Kaplan-Ashiri, I., Alonso, M.-J., Pons-Branchu, E., Dapoigny, A., Rossouw, L., Toffolo, M.B. (2023). New ESR dates from Lovedale, Free State, South Africa: implications for the study of tooth diagenesis. South African Archaeological Bulletin 78(219): 95-103. (DOI not printed in the repository PDF)

conventions.beta_attenuation: Monte Carlo beta attenuation factors from Brennan et al. 1997
conventions.u234_u238_meaning: measured present-day, entered in DATA's U-series screen (the paper reports that US-ESR could not be applied)
conventions.cosmic: Prescott & Hutton 1988 equations; overburden 4.6 ± 1 m; site 28°54'2.35"S, 25°41'7.69"E, 1220 m a.s.l.
conventions.gamma_source: in situ, Canberra Inspector 1000 portable multichannel analyser with NaI(Tl) probe
conventions.software_statement: Ages (1σ) were calculated using the DATA programme (Grün 2009).

samples.provenance: De, dose rates, EU-ESR age: Table 1 (p. 100); sediment U/Th/K, in situ gamma, enamel thickness and removed thickness (side 1 = dentine, side 2 = sediment): Table 2 (p. 101); enamel (E) and dentine (D) U-series: Table 3 (p. 102). Page numbers as reported by the reader for the CENIEH repository PDF.
samples.notes: Published internal dose is printed as 'Enamel (alpha+beta)'. Thickness errors not printed. U-series ratios measured on tissue (present-day activity ratios); not used in EU age model except U concentrations. Depth = 'sediment thickness covering the samples of 4.6 ± 1 m' used for cosmic. Lat/long converted from 28°54'2.35"S, 25°41'7.69"E. LOV2072 and LOV1986 share one in situ gamma measurement. | Verified: cosmic 115 ± 13 µGy/a from the text (gamma+cosmic = in situ gamma + 115). Text says ~20 µm removed per side, Table 2 prints 20–59 µm (table values used).

completeness: partial: only EU-ESR ages (no US/CSUS), no p-values; dose-rate conversion factors not cited; thickness errors and dentine thickness not given; cosmic dose not printed separately (gamma+cosmic only)
extraction_notes: Read twice via WebFetch with different prompts (table-verbatim and per-sample); all values agreed. Water content is printed as 'weight %' (15 ± 5 sediment, 0 enamel, 7 ± 5 dentine) without wet/dry specification. Side 1/side 2 in Table 2 are the thicknesses removed from the dentine and sediment sides respectively ('enamel thickness used to calculate the beta attenuation (side 1 = internal dentine; side 2 = sediment)'). Beta dose from sediment derived from sediment U/Th/K (mass spectrometry).
